searches.note: Twenty one searches of a share of twenty eight, none the author's; one more (Yacochuya's oak) counted to that record. Four were restricted to a house's own domain (bodegacolome.com, elesteco.com.ar, bodegasetchart.com twice, elporvenirwines.com with elporvenirdecafayate.com) and read as primary for the house's own facts. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the grapes, the sites, the making, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.
What a search contradicted was set right with its source; what rested on one source or none was cut or hedged as the house's claim.

tested: Altura Máxima at 3,111 metres at Payogasta and the first vintage 2012: the house's vineyards page, Decanter's sponsored profiles, Liberty Wines, a wine writer's article; agreed. Planting 2004 by one guide, 2007 to 2009 by Decanter: not in the record.

1831 and the founder as governor of Salta in 1809 and 1810: the house's brochure, Wikipedia's list of the intendancy's heads, a Redalyc paper, the argentina.travel page; agreed, his dates not found, so he stays described.
Ownership by the founder's heirs until 2001 and the purchase by a Swiss family: the house and a writer's profile; agreed.
El Arenal and the winery's height: the house's own El Arenal page and sheets give 2,600 and 2,300 metres.
The élevage: the house's sheets for 2016, 2017 and 2019, twenty four months in third and fourth use French oak; no ferment detail anywhere.

tested: 1945, Finca Las Mercedes, six to eight months and three years: the house's Old Vines page, restricted search; agreed.
The Old Vines range and its planting years (Torrontés 1945, Malbec 1946, Cabernet Sauvignon 1947): The Drinks Business, South America Wine Guide's old vine register; agreed.
Pergola vines over seventy years and 239 vines: Decanter alone; the register gives the parcel as more than two hectares, so the count is cut.
Concrete eggs: two writers' notes and The Drinks Business for the old vine wines in general; left out, as the author did.
1892 and the Michel and Torino families, the La Rosa estate, the sales of 1994 and about 2000, Peñaflor in 2004: Wine With Seth, Welcome Argentina, Mercado, a Polish importer's history.

tested: 1850 at La Florida, 1938 and the launch of Arnaldo B. in 1990: the house's English and Spanish pages and its sheets, Bichos de Campo, MDZ; agreed.
The sale to Pernod Ricard in 1996: Bichos de Campo, CellarTracker; agreed beside La Gaceta's 1995.
The buyer of 1938 and his dates: no dates in any source; one piece reports a Don Arnaldo dead in 2017, generation unclear.
The blend: retailers' listings for 2018 and 2019 and MDZ (the rest varying among Tannat, Syrah, Bonarda, Ancellotta, Petit Verdot); the record's wording holds.
The élevage and altitude: the house's sheets, fifteen months in French and American oak (English sheet), first use French oak and 1,750 metres (2020 sheet).

tested: Building in 1998 and the first vintage in February 1999: CellarTracker, Welcome Argentina; agreed.
The partnership of 1987 or 1988 with a Bordeaux consultant and the sale of Etchart in 1996: CellarTracker, Bichos de Campo, La Gaceta's headline; agreed.
Height: 6,700 feet (Wine and Spirits Magazine) and more than 2,000 metres (Welcome Argentina); 2,035 found nowhere.
Vine age: more than sixty years (Welcome Argentina), more than ninety, pre 1950 French material (others); trellised, watered by furrows from springs.
The blend and oak: all Malbec by most, a little Cabernet Sauvignon by one; eighteen months in new French oak for the 2006 and 2015; the second wine 85 per cent Malbec, 15 Cabernet Sauvignon.

it carries the dates the story now gives

open: No site of the estate's own was found; the record stands on secondary sources throughout, and its present ownership is left untold.

tested: Finca El Retiro at 1,650 metres, pergola, sandy alluvial soil, planted 1945 (Torrontés page) or 1950 (vineyards page): the house's two sites, restricted search; agreed as the record gives it.
Concrete eggs and eight months on lees: the de Parcela retailer and the house's sheet, with tasting notes of the El Retiro wine; agreed.

The purchase of 2000, the cellar built by Italian immigrants early in the twentieth century, Tolombón in the late 1970s or the 1980s: Fodor's, ANB Bariloche, Cream Wine, La Gaceta; agreed and hedged as written.
open: The flagship stays the Laborum Torrontés of Finca El Retiro; the integrator may weigh the Porvenir blend, which heads the range, though the El Retiro Torrontés is the wine met abroad.

livingNamesMet: Donald Hess and Ursula Hess (Colomé's buyers of 2001; Ursula Hess may be dead, kept as a guard)
Pablo Etchart (the Etchart family's present generation)
Arnaldo Etchart (the name of the father of 1938 and of the son of Yacochuya; one source has a Don Arnaldo dead in 2017; a guard for prose, the wine's name Arnaldo B. stays)
Roberto Romero (El Porvenir's founder, a former governor of Salta, dead in 1992 by common knowledge, not searched; not named in the record)
Félix Lávaque (El Esteco's buyer of 1994 by one account; not named)

swaps.proposed: none formally; the author's report invites a checker to weigh Porvenir against the Laborum Torrontés of Finca El Retiro
swaps.ruling: refused: the pick stands. The plan names Laborum, the El Retiro Torrontés is the wine importers and critics abroad meet, and a thin region's group is served by teaching the valley's grape from its old pergola vines.

codexTension: The library's Colomé record (p-bodega-colome) speaks of pre-phylloxera vines dating to the 1850s; the house dates its oldest to 1854, so the library is near right but its word pre-phylloxera rests on no source read. Reported, not edited.
The library and the region record give Altura Máxima as roughly 3,100 metres; the house's 3,111 agrees.
